channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: Threats of Political Violence Have America’s Elected Officials Living in Fear
item.description: A Times investigation has found that violent threats have become a new normal among public officials, reshaped private lives, cost millions in security and pushed people out of office.

item.title: NPR: Pope Leo XIV to undergo lung surgery this week
item.description: Pope Leo XIV said he would undergo surgery after doctors found a "localized nodule" in his lung.

item.title: BBC News: Attack on Saudi Arabian airport is another dangerous moment in already tense conflict
item.description: The Houthis have stepped up their attacks on Saudi Arabian soil, and while the physical damage can be quickly repaired, its reputation for stability is taking a battering.

item.title: The Guardian: ‘I want to do everything I can to head off dementia’: why demand for the shingles vaccine is soaring
item.description: Could a drug intended to prevent painful rashes also protect our brains as we get older? The signs are promising – but not conclusive. Yet that’s enough to be driving a boom in shingles jabs When Jenny, a 50-year-old mar…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Power bank fire forces plane to emergency land in India
item.description: A plane flying from Delhi to Chennai made an emergency landing after a power bank reportedly caught fire on board.

item.title: Ars Technica: One with the world? A new look at brains transformed by psychedelics.
item.description: Participants meditated inside an MRI tube, with and without psilocybin.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: Kevin Roose Didn’t Use AI to Write His Book About AI
item.description: The author of The AGI Chronicles says his book “was written by a very tired, overworked, under-slept human being.”

item.title: WIRED Science: How the 2026 Super El Niño and Climate Change Are Related
item.description: Here’s what we know about the record-setting El Niño on a record-hot planet, and the most important questions scientists are trying to answer.

item.title: WIRED Business: I’m Still Convinced the iPod Was the Perfect Gadget
item.description: Apple’s original music player got many things right. Chief among them: It didn’t connect to the internet.

item.title: The New Yorker: What’s Driving the French Student Protests
item.description: A movement born in the Paris banlieues has mobilized young people against diminished school conditions and accumulating problems at home and beyond.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Your Weekly Horoscopes by Madame Clairevoyant: October 11–17
item.description: With Pluto retrograde ending this week, consider how to make a healthy change moving forward.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: Gowanopolis Rising
item.description: You can’t walk an inch in the Brooklyn neighborhood without running into a new luxury tower—or a toxic brownfield.
